paper.title: A minimax and asymptotically optimal algorithm for stochastic bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic K-armed bandit with one-dimensional exponential family arms (bounded means, bounded variance)
unmapped: Variance of the family uniformly bounded by V, giving Pinsker-like inequality kl(mu,mu') >= (mu-mu')^2/(2V)
Means restricted to a fixed interval [mu^-, mu^+] inside the family's mean range
settings.definition_quote: Each arm is assumed to be a probability distribution of some canonical one-dimensional exponential family ... we suppose that each arm $\nu_\theta$ satisfies $\mu=b'(\theta)\in [\mu-,\mu+]\subset I$ ... there exists $V>0$ such that $\sup_{\mu\in I} b''( {b'}^{-1}(\mu))\leq V<+\infty$.

symbols.V_var: uniform upper bound on the variance of distributions in the exponential family
symbols.mu_plus: upper end of the interval containing all arm means
symbols.mu_minus: lower end of the interval containing all arm means

tuning: exploration function g(n) = log_+((T/(K n))(log_+^2(T/(K n)) + 1))

source.label: th:minimax_bound
source.quote: For any family $\mathcal{F}$ satisfying the assumptions detailed in Section~\ref{sec:settings}, and for any bandit model $\nu\in\mathcal{F}$, the expected regret of the kl-UC$\Bpp$ algorithm is upper-bounded as R_T\leq 76 \sqrt{ V K T}+(\mu^+-\mu^-)K\,.

results.notes: Regret defined via means (pseudo-regret). Paper notes the bound also applies to [0,1]-valued rewards with V=1/4.

bound.expression: log(T)/kl_fam(mu_i + delta_p, mu_star - delta_p) + log((1/K)*(1 + log(T/K)**2))/kl_fam(mu_i + delta_p, mu_star - delta_p) + (16*E**2 + 2)*2*V_var*K/delta_p**2 + 1

symbols.kl_fam: KL divergence between members of the exponential family parametrised by their means
symbols.delta_p: free analysis parameter delta of Theorem 2 (not a failure probability)
symbols.V_var: uniform upper bound on the variance of distributions in the exponential family

tuning: exploration function g(n) = log_+((T/(K n))(log_+^2(T/(K n)) + 1))

source.label: th:asymptotic_bound
source.quote: For any bandit model $\nu\in\mathcal{F}$, for any suboptimal arm $a$ and any $\delta$ such that $\sqrt{22 V K / T}\leq \delta\leq(\mustar-\mu_a)/3$, \E[N_a(T)]\leq \frac{\log(T)}{\kl(\mu_a+\delta,\mu^\star-\delta)}+O\left(\frac{\loglog(T)}{\delta^2}\right) which implies the asymptotic optimality (see the end of the proof ... for an explicit bound).

results.notes: Bound on expected number of pulls of a suboptimal arm. Theorem states log(T)/kl(mu_a+delta,mu*-delta) + O(loglog T/delta^2); the expression recorded is the explicit bound given at the end of the proof, which the theorem refers to. Choosing delta ~ (loglog T)^{-1/2} yields asymptotic optimality limsup E[N_a(T)]/log T <= 1/kl(mu_a, mu*), i.e. matching Lai-Robbins.

cited_results.setting_description: Stochastic K-armed bandit, one-dimensional exponential family; uniformly efficient strategies; E[N_a(T)] >= log(T)/kl(mu_a, mu*)(1-o(1)), implying regret lower bound
Minimax lower bound over family F of exponential-family bandits (adaptation of Theorem A.2 of Auer et al.)
